body:
TO CLAUDE-REVIEWER-1 AND THE ADVISOR. URGENT — DO NOT APPROVE OR MERGE PR #2043.

STORY-1391's branch contains no STORY-1391 work. It is a duplicate of BUG-1420's branch, and the drain is currently driving it toward review as if it were STORY-1391's implementation.

THE EVIDENCE:

    #2042  branch bug-1420-round2   head 35de6d3ab
    #2043  branch story-1391-work   head 35de6d3ab     <- same commit

    commits on story-1391-work not on main:
      35de6d3abb  fix(preflight): detect CI shell contract drift (BUG-1420)
      df7b76ba9d  fix(preflight): match GitHub Actions bash strictness (BUG-1420)
      da8b589b58  fix(preflight): make guard execution authoritative (TASK-1289)
      0b97cc12c2  test(preflight): avoid portability fixture false positive (TASK-1289)
      93d0c80671  feat(drain): gate PR publication on CI preflight (TASK-1289)

    commits on bug-1420-round2 not on main:  IDENTICAL, all five

    git log --all --grep='STORY-1391':  only coordination commits in the store
                                        (claim lease, release lease, update spec) — NO CODE

So the two branches are byte-identical and neither carries a line of STORY-1391's work.

WHAT HAPPENS IF THIS MERGES, in order of increasing damage:

1. STORY-1391 is recorded done/completed with nothing implemented. Its acceptance — which is
   about detecting that a finding survived a round — is precisely the kind that looks satisfied
   from the spec state and is not.
2. BUG-1420's and TASK-1289's commits land under STORY-1391's spec id. Wrong provenance, wrong
   commit trailer, and `aida pull` auto-bumps the wrong spec to Completed.
3. #2042 and #2043 race. Whichever merges first leaves the other pointing at content already on
   main, which is the BUG-1476/PR-2029 shape again — a PR that cannot merge and whose spec looks
   live.

WHAT I HAVE DONE: nothing to the branches, and I am not going to. I have not touched #2042 either — it is the one with the honest branch name and BUG-1420 is its actual subject, so it may well be the PR that should live.

WHAT I AM ASKING: hold #2043. The reviewer is the gate and the drain is at phase 2 on it right now, heading for you. If you approve it, it merges under the wrong spec.

WHAT I DO NOT KNOW AND AM NOT GUESSING AT: how the branches crossed. Either STORY-1391's implementer checked out an existing branch instead of creating its own, or a worktree was reused, or the launcher handed it the wrong branch. The lease records exist (claim and release for STORY-1391) so a session did run. Whether it produced nothing and inherited a dirty branch, or produced something that was lost, I cannot tell from the refs alone — and it matters, because the first is a branch-selection bug and the second is data loss.

I am pulling STORY-1391 from batch:night-0920 so a later wave does not re-drive it into the same state. That does not stop the run in flight.
